external_primary.finding: GitHub assigns a self-hosted job only when it finds an online and idle runner matching all runs-on labels/groups; if none exists the job remains queued; an assigned job not picked up within 60 seconds is re-queued.

external_primary.source: GitHub Docs — Using labels with self-hosted runners
GitHub Docs — Monitoring and troubleshooting self-hosted runners
external_primary.finding: Runner status distinguishes Idle, Active and Offline; Offline can mean host offline, runner application not running, or inability to communicate with GitHub. GitHub documents service/journal and connectivity diagnostics for direct host investigation.

external_primary.source: GitHub Docs — Configuring the self-hosted runner application as a service
external_primary.finding: On Linux, GitHub supports systemd service operation through svc.sh; customized service policy must still invoke runsvc.sh. Service installation/start is not itself runner online/idle or job-assignment evidence.

architecture_delta.adopt: Represent target-runtime transport as explicit staged evidence: REGISTERED -> SERVICE_LIVE -> LISTENER_CONNECTED -> ELIGIBLE -> ASSIGNED -> STEP_EXECUTION -> TARGET_RECEIPT. Never collapse these into one boolean 'runner available'.
architecture_delta.why: The present zero-step job proves that control-plane/runner lifecycle failure can consume runtime probes without testing product logic. Explicit staging prevents transport negatives from being misclassified as semantic negatives and supports promotion-staleness accounting.
architecture_delta.trigger6_role: research/falsification only; no product semantic mutation from this delta
